reason: The mechanics are easy: a pure-python post-tail stage of O(forks), about 60 lines like --patch stitch/swapfix, a replay 'fm.*' key after the div_insert block, Kaggle runtime negligible, node count unchanged. But the change AS SPECIFIED conflicts with the DaughterNet insertion that is part of the current base (exp48, probe 28 = 0.948, our only LB-positive division component). The research audit measured the midpoint only on exp39's tail, which has no divinsert forks. The refined_change still applies the rule to 'every 2-child fork' and drops 'the safe-division/divinsert edge' (with steal restore). I measured the inserted forks directly (scratchpad/fm_feas.py: exp39 tail + tools/div_insert.insert_divisions with the replay config s_c4_t0.5 and node_p c785aed28c34eed7; the counts reproduce the replay's +10 TP / +21 FP exactly). Result: 702 inserted forks = 10 TP / 21 FP / 671 free. Inserted TP mid: min 2.86, median 4.16, max 5.94 um. This is expected, because div_insert gates mid <= 6.5 and cos <= 0.25 and does not inherit the symmetric safe-div funnel. At mid >= 4.0 the rule removes 6 of the 10 inserted TP and 15 FP (plus 381 of 671 free forks). The public-calibrated objective is 1.36*(-6) - 0.36*(-21) = -0.60 < 0, and the removed set's precision is 6/21 = 0.29, above the 0.265 break-even. So it would undo most of probe 28's +0.001. At 4.5: 3 TP / 12 FP removed, objective +1.3 but in-sample and noisy. At 3.5: 9 of 10 TP lost. The original 'tighten div_insert mid_um 6.5 -> 4.0' has the same problem. Secondary feasibility gaps: (1) re-checking the threshold 'on the coord-head graph' is not possible in the lab. The cache has fixed detector nodes, and coord-head nodes on the 199 train videos would need a GPU run of exp51 on train. The head moves nodes by 0.74 um on average and up to 1.61 um, while the TP safety margin is 0.24 um (TP max 3.76 vs 4.0). So in a coord-head bundle the threshold is unvalidated. (2) Replay tails keep no safe_division flag (NaN prob = safe-div OR gap/gap2), while the kernel has safe_division=1. The parity rule must be written identically in both. (3) The pre-registered lab gate cannot pass by construction (max about +0.0009), so it cannot be 'tested' in the usual sense, only verified.
fix_if_any: Restrict forkmid to SAFE-DIVISION forks only. Exempt any fork whose added child edge has div_inserted==1: leave divinsert forks alone and drop the steal-restore logic, which then never fires. Identify the added edge in BOTH kernel and replay by the same rule, 'edge_prob is None/NaN and not div_inserted' (the kernel's safe_division==1 is equivalent on TP/FP forks). This keeps kernel/replay parity without re-caching tails. Run it as the last edit, after divinsert, so no divinsert cap slot is freed (non-monotone greedy). Keep div_insert mid_um at 6.5. With that exemption the audited effect holds on exp39: 11 FP / 0 TP at 4.0, objective +3.96. Verify it in one replay pass on the exp48-equivalent base (leaf_prune=0.3 + insert s_c4_t0.5 [+ ef + st]), all 199 videos, on the Kaggle CPU lab. Configs: CTRL, FM40_sdonly, FM45_sdonly, FM40_all (to show the divinsert damage). Criteria: 0 TP lost per embryo, inserted-fork counts identical to CTRL, node count identical. If the next bundle includes the coord head, either leave forkmid out or use >= 4.5 um: the threshold cannot be re-validated on coord-head nodes locally. Ship only inside a bundle; the expected public effect is about +0.001, at LB rounding resolution.
realistic_public_gain: As specified (all forks incl. divinsert, 4.0 um): negative, about -0.0005 to -0.001 (removes about 60% of the inserted TP forks that earned probe 28's +0.001). Repaired (safe-div forks only): about +0.0005 to +0.001 public (3-4 public FP forks x +0.0007 each, minus a 2-4% chance per TP fork of losing a public TP), not separately measurable on the LB; less certain if combined with the coord head.
